findings.kind: correctness / the defect the ticket exists to remove, still live and still untyped
findings.title: One operation key spent on create_prepayment_schedule and then on replace_prepayment_schedule still collides on <key>:plan and still answers the untyped CLR10 — and p1150.namespace.census reads clean on exactly that catalog, because partitionProblems never asks whether two bodies share one suffix
findings.evidence: DRIVEN on clara_c02 through the estate's own doors (scratchpad adv1.mjs). deferredRevenueScene -> createPrepaymentSchedule(opKey=K) admitted (schedule 27398826-e155-48bb-9cb4-8ed3a7d79bb7, plan e07011be-4c5c-4c20-b2a9-c25987442963); receipts: K at create_prepayment_schedule and K:plan at create_accounting_plan. The document term was then corrected through recordPeriod, and replace_prepayment_schedule was called under THE SAME K: `CLR10 op_key reused with different args, detail = null`. That is verbatim the sentence the ticket's Summary complains about ("still collides and still answers an untyped refusal"), naming neither lane nor the derived key, with nothing a surface can classify. Afterwards K:end holds no row at all, so the replacement was refused before it ended anything. The cause is measured, not inferred: the live census (nestedPlanCensus on clara_c02) returns {':plan', 'create_accounting_plan', 'clara._prepayment_schedule_core(...)'} AND {':plan', 'create_accounting_plan', 'clara.replace_prepayment_schedule(...)'} — two bodies, one suffix, one nested fn — and partitionProblems(rows) returns []. Fed a synthetic set with exactly that shape, partitionProblems still returns [] (adv2.mjs): its three rules are 'a suffix no lane declares', 'a body in two lanes' and 'a declared suffix with no deriver', and none of them is 'two derivers of one suffix'. The identical residual exists on the deferred-revenue lane (:rrplan is derived by clara._revenue_recognition_core and clara.replace_revenue_recognition_schedule at the same door). The brief's Desired behavior 1 reads: "No two plan-creating bodies share a nested reservation namespace... and a census cell reads the full list of derivers off the live catalog and fails on any two that share one." The delivered census fails on any two LANES that share one, which is a strictly weaker statement. In fairness: the residual is disclosed in the migration header, in packages/db/README.md's ## 0364 section, and as follow-up 1 of waveK-lane02-ticket1150.md, where it is explicitly recorded as "Measured on the live catalog; not driven" — this review drove it.
findings.required_fix: No code change is owed inside #1150's scope (closing it means recutting two more bodies, which CLOSING-PLAN scopes out). What is owed before the wave closes: (a) file the follow-up ticket the report's follow-up 1 describes, with this driven transcript attached, so the residual stops being a paragraph; (b) either amend #1150's AC2 checkbox to say what the census actually guarantees (one suffix, one LANE) or make partitionProblems ALSO report two derivers of one suffix at one door as a named, currently-expected pair, so the day the follow-up lands the guard is already the one the AC asked for.

findings.kind: instrument sharpness / a census that silently drops what it cannot parse
findings.title: The nested-reservation census reads only `p_op_key || ':x'` sitting directly inside the door call, so a future deriver that wraps the key in a scalar call, or carries it through a local variable, is invisible and the cell still reports problems: []
findings.evidence: DRIVEN against the pure half the cell's own vacuity control uses, derivationsIn() (scratchpad adv2.mjs). `perform clara.create_accounting_plan(p_client, coalesce(p_op_key || ':plan', 'x'))` -> census saw []: enclosingCall returns 'coalesce', which is not in PLAN_DOORS, so the row is dropped by `continue` rather than flagged. `v_key := p_op_key; perform clara.create_accounting_plan(p_client, v_key || ':plan')` -> census saw []: the SQL-side filter and the JS regex both require the literal token `p_op_key`. Controls: the plain form, the named-argument form (what 0353 and 0364 actually write) and the two-derivation form all parse correctly, and an escaped SQL quote earlier in the body (`'this tenancy''s plan'`) does NOT desynchronise maskSql. Nothing on clara_c02 today takes either blind shape, so this is a guard-strength finding and not a live miss. Related brittleness in the same cell: `assert.ok(rows.length >= 10)` will red on the very consolidation ADV-01's follow-up recommends if it ever reduces the number of derivations.
findings.required_fix: Either widen the instrument (walk outwards through non-door enclosing calls to the first PLAN_DOORS name; match `<identifier> || ':x'` and resolve trivially-assigned aliases) or state the limit in the cell's own docstring so a later reader knows a clean census means 'no deriver written in this shape', not 'no deriver'. A one-line note in packages/db/README.md's ## 0364 census paragraph would discharge it.

findings.kind: migration safety / a marker-tolerant pin that admits a body it never wrote
findings.title: 0364's REDO arm accepts ANY body containing the four-character token `0364` anywhere — including inside prose — so a wrong body is admitted as 'my own recut' and would be spliced over without a word
findings.evidence: DRIVEN in two transactions, both rolled back (scratchpad adv6.mjs). ARM 1: 0338's genuine _obo_plan_core statement with one neutral comment injected after `begin` (sha b119eae6) -> the prestate REFUSED by name, CLR10 '... is neither its pinned pre-image (bbe338e8...) nor this file's own recut'. ARM 2: the SAME wrong body with the comment reworded to 'superseded by a later cut; see 0364 for the previous shape' (sha e5768ba0, still neither the pin nor 0364's own 1e366547) -> the prestate raised NOTICE '0364 prestate OK -- 0 FIRST, 6 REDO' and ADMITTED it. The branch is `elsif position('0364' in v_src) > 0`, a bare substring test over the whole body text. Live _obo_plan_core sha was 1e366547 before and after both rollbacks. Blast radius is bounded — CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO only runs against the highest applied version, so 0364 can only be redone while it is the head — and the idiom is the estate's house shape rather than this lane's invention, which is why this is minor and not major.
findings.required_fix: None owed for this wave. If the idiom is carried into the next migration, prefer a marker that cannot occur by accident (the file's own attribution string `#1150 [0364]`, which §A-§F all carry, rather than the bare number), and say in packages/db/README.md's redo note that the marker is a substring test.

findings.kind: test-coverage / an acceptance criterion the cell does not measure
findings.title: AC2 asks for 'exactly one catalog entry with a written meaning' per raised code; the cell only asks whether the code appears as a VALUE, so a future entry with no comment, or two keys mapping to one code, passes all five cells
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/errcode-catalog.test.mjs:99-106 — `const cataloged = new Set(Object.values(CLR)); const missing = [...raised].filter((code) => !cataloged.has(code))`. Nothing reads a comment, so 'with a written meaning' is unmeasured. Nothing compares Object.keys(CLR).length with the distinct value count, so 'exactly one entry' is unmeasured: census_is_exact dedups through `new Set(Object.values(CLR))` before its deepEqual and its `raised.length === 46` assertion, so `foo: 'CLR14'` added beside `dailyLimit: 'CLR14'` leaves all five cells green. Measured on HEAD (scratchpad adv-clr.mjs): 46 keys, 46 distinct values, zero codes carried by two keys, and every entry does carry a meaning — so the state is compliant today and only the guard is missing. (My scanner's one flag, callerContract=CLR44, is a false positive: its meaning is the seven-line block above it.)
findings.required_fix: Two assertions in errcode-catalog.test.mjs: `Object.keys(CLR).length === new Set(Object.values(CLR)).size` (exactly one entry per code, failing by naming the duplicated code), and a source scan of the CLR block requiring each key to carry a `//` comment on its own line or in the lines immediately above it (the written-meaning half), each shown red once against a deliberately broken subject per WORK-ORDER rule 4.

findings.kind: instrument sharpness / a one-declaration guard keyed to one syntactic form
findings.title: clrMapDeclarationSites matches only the exact text `export const CLR = {`, so a second catalog written as `export const CLR = Object.freeze({...})`, `export let CLR = {...}` or `const CLR = {...}; export { CLR };` re-creates the shadowing this ticket exists to remove without failing the cell
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/errcode-catalog.test.mjs:66 — `if (/\bexport\s+const\s+CLR\s*=\s*\{/.test(src)) sites.push(rel);`. `=\s*\{` cannot match `= Object.freeze({`, and `export\s+const` cannot match `export let` or a deferred `export { CLR };` of a locally declared object. The ticket's own AC1 is 'a cell fails if a second declaration appears', not 'a second declaration written this one way'. The cell's vacuity control planted exactly the matching form (`export const CLR = { fake: "CLR98" }`), so the evasions were never exercised. Not live: the scan over the whole packages/db/tests tree returns exactly ['rig-helpers.mjs'] today, and the three modules that carry individual CLR2x constants (wave-a-helpers.mjs, rig-runtime-helpers.mjs, s6-helpers.mjs) are a different pattern the report already discloses as out of scope.
findings.required_fix: Broaden the detector to any top-level binding of the identifier CLR to an object expression (for example `/\b(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+CLR\s*=\s*(?:Object\.freeze\s*\()?\{/` plus a check for a later `export\s*\{[^}]*\bCLR\b`), and show it red once against one of the evading forms.

findings.kind: consistency / two doors recut in one file answer the same mistake differently
findings.title: §A wraps clara._reserve_op's detail-less CLR10 with a typed op_key_conflict; §C, recut in the same migration, still lets the raw 'op_key reused with different args' out with detail = null
findings.evidence: DRIVEN (scratchpad adv5.mjs) on clara_c02. create_accrual_adjustment, same key with a different amount: CLR10 'this accrual key already configured a DIFFERENT accrual', detail {"reason":"op_key_conflict","field":"op_key"}. confirm_tenancy_rent_plan, same key with a different payable account: CLR10 'op_key reused with different args', detail null. Both are the OUTER reservation on the caller's own key, not the nested one #1150 is about, and typing clara._reserve_op's raise is explicitly out of scope for this ticket (#1077 follow-up 2) — so this is not a regression and not a scope breach. It is worth recording because #1150 is the file that had both bodies open at once, and a surface written against the accrual door's typed answer will get nothing to render from the tenancy door for the identical mistake.
findings.required_fix: None in this wave. Worth adding to the #1077-follow-up-2 ticket as a concrete pair of measured answers, so whoever types the primitive knows which doors already wrap it and which do not.

summary: Seven adversarial probes were run against lane L2's diff (ffb629d73...20e73c102, 15 files, all under packages/db). The migration itself stands up to attack: all six prestate pins re-derive exactly from the creating migrations' own text; the FIRST-APPLY arm was proved in a rolled-back transaction (6 FIRST / 0 REDO) against genuinely restored pre-images; real drift refuses by name; §A-§E are minimal verbatim recuts with nothing dropped; §F's fold carries every wall, lock, insert, advisory, audit verb, `via` and return key of the body it replaces, and its one disclosed divergence is unreachable on an ungranted body with a single literal-passing caller; tenant isolation and the no-existence-oracle rule hold on all three recut doors across two firms with nothing written by any refusal; grants, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, volatility and search_path all survive the replace; and neither §0 nor §TAIL reads a row, so nothing can mis-apply on a populated hosted database. The frozen law is clean and `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` was re-run to exit 0. The one finding that matters is ADV-01: the exact defect #1150 exists to remove is still live inside the prepayment lane — one key spent on create_prepayment_schedule and then on replace_prepayment_schedule collides on <key>:plan and is answered `CLR10 op_key reused with different args` with no detail at all — and the census the brief asked for ("fails on any two that share one") is a lane-level guard that reads clean on exactly that catalog. The lane disclosed this in the migration header, the README and its own follow-up 1, and said it was "not driven"; this review drove it. The remaining six findings are guard-strength, documentation and consistency items, none of them live defects.
